Extensions (windvg.ext)¶

The core stays small; richer tools live in windvg.ext.

Transforms¶

Transform is an immutable affine matrix. transformed(shape, t) bakes one into a new shape; translated / rotated / scaled / mirrored_x / mirrored_y are shorthands.

Transforms respect the shape model: circles under uniform transforms stay circles; under non-uniform scaling they become exact ellipses; warped arcs become exact elliptical-arc paths.

from windvg.ext import Transform

gear = gear.transformed(Transform.rotate(15, about=center))

Repetition¶

  • sample(shape, n, offset) — n evenly spaced points along any track,

  • along(track, motifs, n, align="tangent") — place motifs around a track, optionally rotated to follow it: petals, gear teeth, rosettes,

  • polar(center, motifs, n, radius) — motifs on a circle,

  • grid(motifs, cols, rows, dx, dy) — a lattice of motifs.

from windvg.ext import along

petal = wv.Ellipse((0, -20), 12, 20)   # built pointing up from the origin
for placed in along(circle, [petal], 8, align="tangent"):
    scene.fill(placed, wv.rgb(0.95, 0.8, 0.2))

Rounded corners¶

rounded(polygon, radius) replaces every corner with an exact arc fillet — a fillable Path, not a polyline approximation.

from windvg.ext import rounded

badge = rounded(wv.regular_polygon(center, 80, 6), 12)
scene.fill(badge, wv.rgb(0.3, 0.55, 0.95))

API¶

.. py:module:: windvg.ext

Optional extensions on top of the windvg core.

Everything here is importable from the main package namespace of your own code, e.g.::

   from windvg.ext import Transform, transformed, along

.. py:class:: Transform(a: float = 1.0, b: float = 0.0, c: float = 0.0, d: float = 1.0, e: float = 0.0, f: float = 0.0) :module: windvg.ext :canonical: windvg.ext.transform.Transform

Bases: :py:class:object

A 2D affine transform: x’ = ax + cy + e, y’ = bx + dy + f.

.. py:method:: Transform.rotate(angle_deg: float, about: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point = (0.0, 0.0)) -> ~windvg.ext.transform.Transform :module: windvg.ext :classmethod:

  Rotation clockwise on screen for positive angles, around `about`.

.. py:method:: Transform.mirror_x(axis: float = 0.0) -> ~windvg.ext.transform.Transform :module: windvg.ext :classmethod:

  Reflect across the vertical line x = axis.

.. py:method:: Transform.mirror_y(axis: float = 0.0) -> ~windvg.ext.transform.Transform :module: windvg.ext :classmethod:

  Reflect across the horizontal line y = axis.

.. py:property:: Transform.is_similarity :module: windvg.ext :type: bool

  True for uniform scale + rotation + translation (angle-preserving).

.. py:function:: along(track, motifs: ~collections.abc.Sequence[~windvg.shapes.Shape], n: int, offset_pct: float = 0.0, align: str | None = ‘tangent’, direction: ~windvg.shapes.Orientation = Orientation.CW) -> list[~windvg.shapes.Shape] :module: windvg.ext

Place the motifs n times around the track.

With align="tangent" each copy is rotated so its +x axis follows the track’s travel direction; with align=None copies keep their original orientation.

.. py:function:: grid(motifs: ~collections.abc.Sequence[~windvg.shapes.Shape], cols: int, rows: int, dx: float, dy: float, origin: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point = (0.0, 0.0)) -> list[~windvg.shapes.Shape] :module: windvg.ext

Place the motifs on a cols x rows lattice with spacing dx, dy.

.. py:function:: polar(center: tuple[float, float] | ~windvg.geometry.Point, motifs: ~collections.abc.Sequence[~windvg.shapes.Shape], n: int, radius: float, start_deg: float = 0.0, align: str | None = None) -> list[~windvg.shapes.Shape] :module: windvg.ext

Place the motifs n times on a circle around center.

.. py:function:: rounded(shape: ~windvg.shapes.Polygon, radius: float) -> ~windvg.path.Path :module: windvg.ext

A Path tracing the polygon with each corner replaced by a fillet arc.

The result fills (and strokes) exactly: corners become real arc instructions, not polyline approximations. The radius must leave at least half of every edge straight.

.. py:function:: sample(shape, n: int, offset_pct: float = 0.0, direction: ~windvg.shapes.Orientation = Orientation.CW) -> list[~windvg.geometry.Point] :module: windvg.ext

n evenly spaced points along the shape’s track.

Closed tracks place points i*100/n apart (the last point is not the first point again); open tracks include both endpoints.

.. py:function:: transformed(shape: Shape, t: Transform) -> Shape :module: windvg.ext

Bake an affine transform into a new shape.
